query:
The profiler is installed as a dev dependency and bundled in ProfilingModule. The app added @nestjs/graphql + @nestjs/apollo + graphql with GraphQLModule.forRoot() (context not customized).

User: Add the GraphQL collector.
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-simple.md. Install '<pm> add -D @eleven-labs/nest-profiler-graphql' and register GraphQLCollectorModule.forRoot() (the module is GraphQLCollectorModule, NOT ProfilerGraphQLModule) in the ProfilingModule bundle, no gate. Apply the gotcha: the app's GraphQLModule context must expose the request — for Apollo, context: ({ req }) => ({ req }) — plain app config that stays in the production module; without it, GraphQL operations are not profiled.

query: Which collector is ESM-only and what does that imply for wiring it?
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-orm.md. Answer: nest-profiler-mikro-orm is the only ESM-only collector ('type': 'module', .js import specifiers). It must be imported after MikroOrmModule; it wraps the ORM logger on init and needs no dataSource.

query: I installed the HTTP collector but nothing shows up in the HTTP Client panel. Why?
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-http.md. Answer: nothing is captured unless an instrumentation is listed — HttpCollectorModule.forRoot({ instrumentations: [AxiosInstrumentation] }) (from '@eleven-labs/nest-profiler-http/axios'), with HttpModule imported in the SAME module. For fetch use FetchInstrumentation (from '/fetch'); for undici/got inject HttpProfilerRecorder and call .capture(...) or provide a custom HttpInstrumentation.

query: Can I keep my existing global ValidationPipe when I add the validator collector?
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-validator.md. Answer: Yes — validation stays app-owned, just wrap the existing pipe with createProfilerValidationPipe(yourPipe) where the profiler is loaded: with the dev-dependency install, through a validationPipe hook of the shared bootstrap passed by main-dev.ts only (production keeps the plain pipe); with the ConditionalModule install, in main.ts. For class-validator wrap createClassValidatorPipe(options) instead of a bare ValidationPipe so per-property violations reach the panel. Then register the panel with ValidatorCollectorModule.forRoot() in the ProfilingModule bundle. Only one global validation pipe; use value imports (not 'import type') for DTOs.

query: The app just added TypeORM. Do I need forRootAsync with inject: [DataSource] to add the collector?
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-orm.md. Answer: No — TypeOrmCollectorModule self-resolves the DataSource via getDataSourceToken(connectionName), so forRoot() is enough (use forRootAsync only to read options like slowThreshold from ConfigService). Register it in the ProfilingModule bundle, matching the app's existing install; optionally add TypeOrmSchemaCollectorModule for the entity panel.

query:
package.json includes @nestjs/config and @nestjs/event-emitter. The app emits domain events with emitAsync and reacts to them with @OnEvent.

User: I want to see what my domain events actually do.
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-simple.md. Offer nest-profiler-event-emitter with EventEmitterCollectorModule.forRoot() placed alongside EventEmitterModule.forRoot() (infra-scoped, not the root), gated like the core. Explain the three surfaces: the Events panel on the emitting profile, the Discover / Events view, and one `event` profile per @OnEvent execution (profileListeners, on by default). Must flag the request-scoped-subscriber limitation and that @OnEvent suppresses handler errors by default.
